Toxic

/TAWK-sik/ — stress on TAWK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Toxic describes something poisonous or harmful to living things.

The old factory left toxic chemicals buried in the riverbed.

Worked Example

After the snake bite, the venom flowed through the hiker's arm; the wound site became swollen and toxic within hours.

tox (poison) + -ic (having the character of) = poisonous or having poison's destructive quality. The swollen wound literally contains the poison from the snake, so toxic precisely describes a site where poison is actively present and harmful.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

poisonous: containing a poison that sickens if swallowed or touched; toxic is the broader, official word for hazards, as in toxic waste

harmful: causing damage of any kind, mild or severe

noxious: harmful, especially fumes or gases you breathe

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

harmless: unable to cause any hurt or damage

benign: gentle and doing no harm at all

Where it sits · how dangerous it is to your body — unpleasant → unhealthy → harmful → toxic

unpleasant vs. toxic: A smell can be unpleasant without hurting you at all, but a toxic fume can actually poison you.

unhealthy vs. toxic: Junk food is unhealthy if you eat it every day, while a toxic chemical can damage your body after a single exposure.

harmful vs. toxic: Too much sun is harmful to your skin, but swallowing a toxic substance is far more dangerous.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tox

Root — tox: poison — from Greek toxikon, 'arrow poison', from toxon, 'bow' (Greek)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of; having the nature of (Greek (via Latin -icus))

Put it together

Put it together: tox- (poison) + -ic (characteristic of) = having the nature of poison. Ancient Greek archers dipped their arrowheads in poison, so toxikon — 'arrow poison', from toxon, 'bow' — became the word for poison itself.

Use the root in a new word: toxin

Use the root in a new word: toxin: Some snakes protect themselves with a toxin powerful enough to paralyze a much larger animal.

Word Choice

neutral/clinical

Reach for toxic when something contains actual poison, causes real harm, or is deeply damaging — in substance, environment, or human behavior. It's stronger than 'bad' or 'unpleasant' and implies a genuine hazard.
